500656:
Last reviewed: Friday 23 Oct 2026 at 10.01am

There will be evening track closures from 7:45pm on the Shorncliffe line to allow testing of the new European Train Control System (ETCS) throughout 2026 and into 2027.

During these closures, trains will not run between Northgate and Shorncliffe stations.

Please note that additional works for these closures are being considered. Further dates may be added once confirmed.

October evening closures (from 7:45pm)

  • Monday 26 to Thursday 29 October

November evening closures (from 7:45pm)

  • Monday 2 to Thursday 5 November
  • Monday 9 and Tuesday 10 November
  • Thursday 12 November
  • Monday 16 and Tuesday 17 November
  • Monday 23 and Tuesday 24 November
  • Thursday 26 November
  • Monday 30 November

Track closures on the Shorncliffe line may be subject to change. Please check again closer to your travel time.

Until Monday 2 November the railbus stop for Northgate station will be temporarily located on Melton Road, due to roadworks.

Map of closure

Travel information

During these closures, timetabled railbuses will replace trains between Northgate and Shorncliffe stations to get you where you need to be. 

  • Railbus R348 will stop at all stations between Northgate and Shorncliffe stations and will depart approximately every 30 minutes. 

Shorncliffe line trains will continue to run between Northgate and Roma Street stations. 

Please allow extra travel time and plan your journey closer to the travel date using our journey planner, which is being updated as quickly as possible.

Bikes and e-scooters are not permitted on railbuses. 

What works are happening?

Cross River Rail is testing the new world-class signalling system, the European Train Control System (ETCS), on the Shorncliffe line. Testing ETCS to confirm the system meets safety regulations and operational requirements is an important step before testing in the Cross River Rail tunnels can commence.

During this period, you may see trains travelling on the Shorncliffe line and stopping at some stations. These trains are undergoing important testing and are not in service.

For more information on the Cross River Rail project, visit the Cross River Rail website. 

Ticket and fare information

Normal fares and conditions apply on all scheduled services.
